source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)

verses.translation: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Caesar Tiberius, when Pontius Pilatus [was] governor [or: possessor of authority] in Judea, and Herod [was] tetrarch of the Galilee region, and Philip, brother of Herod, [was] tetrarch of the kingdom [or: domain] of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias [was] tetrarch of Abilene

translation_notes: חמש (consonants חמש): Candidates: H2567 'to tax a fifth', H2568 'five', H2569 'a fifth tax', H2570 'abdomen', H2571 'able-bodied soldiers'. Chose H2568 'five' because context is a numerical date ('year of five ten' = fifteenth year).
מורשה (consonants מורשה): Only candidate H4181 'a possession'. In context of a Roman governor appointed over Judea, the sense is 'one who holds possession/authority' — functioning as 'governor'.
אח (consonants אח): Candidates: H251 'brother', H252 'brother', H253 'Oh!', H254 'fire-pot', H255 'howler'. Chose H251 because Philip is identified as the brother of Herod, a familial relationship.
ממלכות (consonants ממלכות): Candidates: H4468 'dominion/realm', H4438 'a rule/dominion'. Chose H4468 because the context describes a territorial domain (Ituraea and Trachonitis).
textual_notes: The word מורשה (H4181 'possession') is used here to render the concept of a Roman governor/procurator — an unusual Hebrew rendering suggesting 'one who holds authority/possession' over a province.
Several words are transliterations of Latin/Greek names (קיסר, טברי, פילאט, הורדוס, טטרקא, פליף, איטוראה, טרכנה, לישניאה, אבילינה) with no Strong's numbers.
The consonants ש נת could be parsed as שנת (construct of שנה 'year') or as separate particles ש + נת. The year-of construction fits the dating formula.

verses.literal: In year [of] five ten to Caesar Tiberius and Pontius Pilatus governor in Judah and Herodius tetrarch from Galilee and Philip brother [of] Herodius tetrarch [of] kingdom [of] Ituraea and Trachonitis and Lysanias [of] Abilene tetrarch

verses.translation: Under [the authority of] the chief priests, [with] Caiaphas presiding [or: officiating], the word [or: commission] of God came upon Yochanan [John] son of Zechariah in the wilderness [or: open country]

translation_notes: תחת (consonants תחת): Candidates: H8478 'underneath/under', H8479 same, H8480 'Tachath' (proper noun). Chose H8478 because context describes a hierarchical authority — 'under the chief priests.'

שרי (consonants שרי): Candidates: H8297 'Sarai', H8298 'Sharay', or שר (H8269) 'chief/prince' in construct plural. Chose שרי as construct plural of שר 'chiefs/princes' because it modifies הכהנים 'the priests' — yielding 'chiefs of the priests' (high priestly authority).
מאל (consonants מ+אל): Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 'God' because the context describes a divine commission/word coming from God.

במדבר (consonants ב+מדבר): Candidates: H4057 'wilderness/pasture/desert', or ב+דבר H1697 'in [the] word/matter'. Chose H4057 'wilderness' because the physical location of Yochanan's activity is being specified.
textual_notes: The separation 'נ ע&שת המילה' is puzzling. It could be read as נעשת 'was done/made' (nifal of עשה) with 'the word' — i.e., 'the word was made/established.' The נ may be a nifal prefix separated in the manuscript.
הולך בקיפא could mean 'walking in Caiaphas' (i.e. Caiaphas was the one officiating/serving) or 'going to Caiaphas.' The participial form suggests an ongoing state — Caiaphas was the one presiding.
המילה could be read as 'the word' (from מלה) or 'the circumcision' (from מילה). In context of a divine commission, 'the word' is more coherent.

verses.literal: Under princes [of] the priests walking in Caiaphas was the doing [of] the word from God upon Yochanan son [of] Zechariah in the wilderness

verses.translation: And Yochanan [John] came into all the region [or: domain] of Judea, proclaiming [or: seeking out] immersion of repentance [or: returning] for the forgiveness [or: pardoning] of the iniquities of the sinners

translation_notes: בכל (consonants ב+כל): H3605 'the whole/all' with prefix ב 'in'. Straightforward: 'in all.'
ממלכות (consonants ממלכות): Candidates: H4468 'dominion/realm', H4438 'rule/dominion'. Chose H4468 — the concrete sense 'country/realm' fits describing the geographic region of Judah.
תשובה (consonants תשובה): H8666 'a recurrence/return/reply'. Here used in the moral sense of 'returning' (repentance), which is the standard later Hebrew usage of this root.
textual_notes: דורש could be from דרש 'to seek/inquire/demand' — here functioning as a participle meaning 'proclaiming' or 'advocating.' No Strong's candidates were provided but the root דרש (H1875) fits.
טבילת and מחילת are construct forms of post-biblical Hebrew words (טבילה 'immersion' and מחילה 'forgiveness') not found in the Strong's Hebrew lexicon, suggesting a later Hebrew composition.
החוטאים 'the sinners' — this could modify עונות ('iniquities of the sinners') or stand independently. The construct chain suggests 'iniquities of the sinners.'

verses.literal: And came Yochanan in all [the] kingdom [of] Judah seeking immersion [of] returning for forgiveness [of] iniquities [of] the sinners

verses.translation: Just as [it is] written in the book [or: scroll] of the words of Isaiah the prophet: A voice calling out in the wilderness [or: open land] — Clear the way of the Mighty One [God], make his paths straight. [Marginal notes: Fifteen — five and ten — years; Tiberius (variant spellings); Caesar (variant spellings); Pontius; tetrarch; governor or tetrarch]

translation_notes: בספר (consonants ב+ספר): Candidates: H5608 'to inscribe', H5609 'a book', H5612 'writing/book', H5613 'scribe'. Chose H5612 'a book/scroll' because the preposition ב + noun 'book' yields 'in the book,' matching the context of a written prophetic text.
דרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 'way/road' because it is the object of פנו 'clear' — 'clear the way.'

האל (consonants ה+אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 'God' with definite article ה — 'the God/the Mighty One.' This fits the prophetic quotation about preparing God's way.
עשר (consonants עשר): Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6240 'ten in combination (-teen)'. Chose H6240 because combined with חמשה it yields 'fifteen.'
תרשתא (consonants תרשתא): H8660 'Tirshatha — title of a Persian governor.' Used here as a Hebrew gloss for 'governor,' explaining the foreign term 'tetrarch.'
textual_notes: The latter portion of this section (from ט״ו onward) appears to be marginal glosses or scribal annotations, not continuous text. Multiple variant spellings of Tiberius (טיברי/טברי) and Caesar (שיזאר/שיסאר) suggest a scribe working through transliteration options.
קורא could be the proper name Kore (H6981) or a participle of קרא 'to call/cry out.' The prophetic context ('a voice calling in the wilderness') strongly favors the verbal participle.
The relationship between תרשתא and טטררך suggests the scribe glossed the foreign word 'tetrarch' with the known Hebrew term for a foreign governor (Tirshatha).
דברי could be the proper name Dibri (H1704) or the construct plural of דבר 'word.' Context ('book of the words of Isaiah') demands the latter.

verses.literal: As [is] written in [the] book [of] words [of] Isaiah the prophet a voice calling in the wilderness clear [the] way [of] the God make straight his paths. Fifteen five ten years Tiberius Tiberius Tiberius Caesar Caesar Pontius tetrarch governor or tetrarch

verses.translation: Every valley will be filled up, and every mountain and hill will be brought low [or: humbled], and all the crooked [or: bad] paths will be made straight [or: directed], and all the rough ridges [will become] smooth [or: level] roads

translation_notes: כל (consonants כל): H3605 and H3606 are identical in meaning ('the whole/all'). H3605 is the standard Hebrew form; H3606 is Aramaic. Chose H3605 for Hebrew context.
textual_notes: מיו<רים contains an unclear character (<). It likely represents מיושרים 'made straight/directed' (from ישר via pual/hophal participle), with the < possibly being a damaged or uncertain letter in the manuscript.

רעים could be from רע 'bad/evil' (describing crooked paths) or from רעע 'to break/shatter' (describing rough terrain). Both produce coherent images in this leveling-landscape context; 'bad/crooked' fits the parallel with ישרים 'straight.'

verses.literal: All the valleys will be filled and all the mountains and the hills will be brought low and all the ways bad will be made straight and all the rough places to ways smooth

verses.translation: And all flesh [or: all humanity] will see the salvation [or: peace, wholeness] of the Mighty One [God]

translation_notes: בשר (consonants בשר): Candidates: H1319 'to announce glad news', H1320 'flesh/body/person', H1321 same. Also שר H8269 'chief' with prefix ב. Chose H1320 'flesh' because 'all flesh' is a standard Hebrew idiom for all humanity, and it is the subject of 'will see.'

שלום (consonants שלום): Candidates: H7965 'safe/welfare/health/prosperity/peace', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum' (name). Chose H7965 'peace/welfare/salvation' because the context is a prophetic promise of God's saving action visible to all humanity.
האל (consonants ה+אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 'God' with definite article — 'the God.' The salvation/peace belongs to God.
textual_notes: שלום here could mean 'peace,' 'welfare,' 'wholeness,' or 'salvation.' The Hebrew word carries a broader semantic range than any single English equivalent. The prophetic context (Isaiah quotation) typically carries the sense of God's saving deliverance, but the Hebrew consonants support the full range of שלום — peace, completeness, wholeness, prosperity.

verses.literal: And will see all flesh salvation [of] the God

verses.translation: Then he said to the crowds [or: peoples] who came so that he would immerse them: Offspring [or: generations] of vipers — who taught you to flee from the wrath [or: burning anger from our nostrils] that is about to come?
words: in order that/for the sake of
to flee / in spirit / in wind

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 'to say' — the verb form fits 'then he said.'

בעבור (consonants ב+עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain.' Chose H5668 because the context describes the purpose for which the crowds came — so that he would immerse them.

למד (consonants למד): Candidates: H3925 'to teach/goad'. Also מד H4055 'a measure/garment.' Chose H3925 'taught' because the question 'who taught you to flee' makes coherent sense as a rhetorical challenge.

ברוח (consonants ב+רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room', H7306 'to smell/blow', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit'. This could mean 'to flee' (reading ברוח as infinitive of ברח 'to flee' with different vocalization) or 'in/by spirit/wind.' Given the question 'who taught you to flee from the coming wrath,' reading ברוח as לברוח 'to flee' produces the most coherent image.
textual_notes: ברוח is highly ambiguous: it could be (1) from ברח 'to flee' (infinitive with ב prefix), (2) ב + רוח 'in/by wind/spirit' (H7307), or (3) related to ריח 'smell/perceive.' The flee reading produces the most natural sentence: 'who taught you to flee from the coming wrath?'

מאפינו is difficult. It could be מ + אף + ינו 'from our nostrils/anger' (אף = nose/anger + 1cp suffix), yielding 'from our wrath.' Alternatively it could be a form related to 'baking' (אפה). The wrath/anger reading fits the context of fleeing from coming judgment.
תולדות could mean 'generations/descendants' or 'offspring' — both work for describing those born of vipers.
פתנים — likely plural of פתן 'viper/asp' (cf. H6620). No Strong's candidate was provided but the consonants match the known Hebrew word for venomous serpent.

verses.literal: Then he said to the peoples who came in order that he would immerse them offspring [of] vipers who taught to you to flee from the wrath the coming to come

verses.translation: Therefore produce fruits worthy of [your] immersion [or: repentance], and do not begin to say: Our father — he [is] Abraham! I say to you that the Mighty One [God] is able from these stones to bring back to life [or: restore] a living son of Abraham

translation_notes: עשו (consonants עשו): H6215 'Esau' (proper name). However, in context this is clearly an imperative plural of עשה 'to do/make' — 'do/produce [fruits].' The consonants match Esau's name coincidentally but the grammatical function is verbal imperative.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/she/it', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist.' Chose H1931 as the emphatic pronoun 'he [is]' — identifying Abraham as father.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship.' Chose H589 'I' because the speaker is making a first-person declaration.
שהאל (consonants ש+ה+אל): ש is relative particle 'that' + ה definite article + אל. Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H410 'God'. Chose H410 'God' — 'that the God [is able].'

החזיר (consonants החזיר): Candidates: H2386 'hog/pig', H2387 'Chezir' (name). However, this is almost certainly the hifil infinitive/verb of חזר 'to return/restore' — 'to cause to return/restore.' The hog reading would produce: 'the pig alive son of Abraham' which is incoherent. The causative 'to restore/bring back' fits perfectly.
חי (consonants חי): Candidates: H2416 'alive/living', H2417 same (Aramaic). Chose H2416 — 'alive/living' modifying 'son.'

אלו (consonants אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if.' Context suggests 'these' (demonstrative pronoun, a common later Hebrew form). H431 'lo!' can function demonstratively. Chose H431 as 'these.'
לאמר (consonants ל+אמר): H559 'to say' with prefix ל (infinitive construct). Standard Hebrew construction meaning 'to say/saying.'
textual_notes: החזיר is the most significant ambiguity: the consonants match both חזיר 'pig/hog' (H2386) and the hifil of חזר 'to return/restore.' The verbal reading ('to restore alive') produces a coherent theological statement; the noun reading ('the pig alive') does not.
א בינו — the א could be an abbreviation for אב 'father' with בינו meaning 'our father,' or א could be a separate particle. The combined reading 'our father' fits the declaration about Abraham.
עשו matches both the imperative of עשה and the proper name Esau (H6215). Context demands the verb.

verses.literal: Therefore do fruits worthy from immersion and not begin to say our father he [is] Abraham I say to you that the God is able from stones these to return alive a son [of] Abraham

verses.translation: For the axe has already been laid [or: passed through] to the root of the tree; therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and cast [or: placed] into the fire

translation_notes: כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that.' Chose H3588 because this introduces a causal explanation — 'for the axe already...'

כבר (consonants כבר): Candidates: H3527 'to augment/multiply', H3528 'long ago/already/formerly', H3529 'Kebar river.' Also בר candidates. Chose H3528 'already' because it modifies the verb — the axe has already been laid to the root.

עברה (consonants עברה): Candidates: H5678 'an outburst of passion/wrath', H5679 'a crossing-place.' However this is most likely the 3fs perfect of עבר 'to cross/pass over' — 'has passed/been laid.' The axe has crossed over to the root. Neither noun candidate fits as well as the verbal reading.
טוב (consonants טוב): Candidates: H2895 'to be/do good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness (noun).' Chose H2896 adjective 'good' modifying fruit.

באש (consonants ב+אש): Candidates for באש: H887 'to smell bad', H889 'stench.' Candidates for אש: H784 'fire', H787 'foundation.' Chose ב + אש H784 'in fire' — trees cast into fire is the coherent image. 'In a stench' would be bizarre here.
לכן (consonants ל+כן): H3651 'so/thus' with prefix ל yielding 'therefore.' Standard Hebrew conjunction.
textual_notes: עברה could be parsed as a noun (H5678 'wrath' or H5679 'crossing-place') or as a 3fs perfect verb from עבר 'to pass/cross.' The verbal reading ('has passed/been set') is most natural with 'the axe' as subject.

verses.literal: For the axe already has passed to [the] root [of] the tree therefore every tree that does not make fruit good will be cut and will be placed in fire

verses.translation: And the crowds [or: peoples] asked him, saying: If so, what shall we do?

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether/although.' Chose H518 'if' because the phrase אם כן 'if so' is a standard Hebrew conditional expression introducing a question.
כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/upright', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat.' Chose H3651 'so/thus' — paired with אם to form 'if so.'
מה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what?/how?/why?', H4101 same (Aramaic). Chose H4100 — interrogative 'what?'

יעשו (consonants יעשו): H3299 'Jaasu' (proper name). However, this is clearly the 3mp imperfect of עשה 'to do/make' — 'shall they do?' or 'shall we do?' The proper name reading is contextually impossible.
textual_notes: יעשו could be 3mp 'shall they do' or understood as 1cp in sense ('what shall we do') given that the crowds are asking about themselves. The 3mp form is literal but the intent is self-referential.

verses.literal: And the peoples asking him saying if so what shall they do

verses.translation: And he responded, saying: Be satisfied [or: filled up] — let yourselves be filled — and draw near and trust him. Whoever has two garments, let him give to the one who has none. And whoever has shares [or: exchanges] of wealth, let him do this also in the same way.

translation_notes: ענה (ע-נ-ה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond', H6031 'to depress', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because the context is a dialogue — he is responding to a question or situation.

שיש (ש-י-ש): Candidates: H7893 'marble', H3426 (יש) 'there is'. The ש is a relative prefix ('who/that'), and יש means 'there is', yielding 'who has' — this fits the context of possessing garments perfectly.

שני (ש-נ-י): Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'two/second'. Chose H8145 'two' because the sentence is about sharing garments — 'two garments' makes perfect sense while 'crimson garments' would be oddly specific.
אחד (א-ח-ד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one'. Chose H259 'one' — the person who lacks even one garment.
זה (ז-ה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 'this' as the demonstrative pronoun pointing to the same action of giving.
כן (כ-נ): Candidates: H3651 'so/likewise', H3653 'a stand', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 'likewise/so' as an adverb completing 'also likewise'.
textual_notes: The sequence תתמלאו יתמלאו תתמלאו ת תתמלאנה יתמלאו appears to be a scribal difficulty — possibly multiple attempts at copying a single verb form, or a textual corruption. The repeated forms alternate between 2mp and 3mp/3fp, which is unusual. The isolated ת may be an abbreviation or a fragment. This entire sequence is highly uncertain.
חלופי העושרים: 'portions/exchanges of the riches' — חלופי derives from ח-ל-ף (to exchange/change). It could mean 'surplus provisions' or 'exchangeable wealth'. The exact nuance is ambiguous.
The word אומר is listed only as H201 'Omar' (a proper name), but in context it clearly functions as a participle of אמר (H559) 'saying'. The lexicon entry provided is incomplete.

verses.literal: And he answered saying be filled let them be filled be filled ... let them be filled let them be filled and draw near and trust him who has to him two garments let him give to whoever does not have to him one and whoever has to him portions of the riches let him do this also likewise

verses.translation: And the worldly people [or: tax collectors, people of the world] came in order to be immersed [baptized], and they said, 'Rabbi, what should we do?'
words: in order that / for the sake of

translation_notes: מה (מ-ה): Candidates: H4100, H4101 — both mean 'what?'. Chose H4100 as the standard interrogative.
יעשו: Listed only as H3299 'Jaasu' (a name), but contextually this is clearly a 3mp imperfect of עשה (H6213) 'to do'. The provided lexicon entry is a name sharing the same consonants.
textual_notes: העולמיים — 'the worldly ones': This is not a standard biblical Hebrew term. It appears to be a later Hebrew formation from עולם (world/age) with a gentilic/adjectival suffix. It likely refers to people involved in worldly affairs — possibly tax collectors or secular officials. The exact referent is uncertain.

verses.literal: And came the worldly ones in order that they would be immersed and they said Rabbi what shall we do

verses.translation: And he responded to them: Do not do [anything] beyond [or: more than] only what you have been given authority [to do].

translation_notes: ענה (ע-נ-ה): Chose H6030 'to respond' — he is answering their question.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1992 (הם) 'them'. With ל prefix, this is 'to them' — standard indirect object. Chose H1992.
לא (ל-א): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 (Aramaic 'not'). Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
עוד (ע-ו-ד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify', H5750 'more/again', H5751 (same as 5750). Chose H5750 'more' — 'do not do more' fits the instruction to restrain their actions.
לבד (ב-ד with ל prefix): H905 'separation/alone/only'. 'Only' works perfectly — 'do not do more, only what...'
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', or כ + מה (H4100) 'as/how much'. Chose the compound reading כ + מה = 'as much as', which fits the instruction about limits of authority.
שנתן: ש (relative 'that') + נתן H5414 'was given'. Passive sense from context — 'that was given to you.'
textual_notes: רשות is a post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'authority/permission', not found in the Strong's biblical lexicon. It confirms the later Hebrew provenance of this text.

verses.literal: And he answered to them do not do more only as much as was given to you authority

verses.translation: And the soldiers [or: horsemen] asked him, saying, 'What should we do?' And Yochanan said: Do not desire [or: delight in] evil toward any person, and do not cause him harm [or: loss], and be generous [or: noble-hearted] with your wages.

translation_notes: אמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — Yochanan is speaking.
אל: Candidates: H408 'do not (deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 — this is a negative imperative 'do not desire'.

רע (ר-ע): Candidates: H7451 'evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 'evil' — 'do not desire evil to any person' is a coherent moral instruction.
לשום: ל + שום. Candidates: H7760 'to put/place', H7762 'garlic'. H7760 in the sense of 'any' (as in לשום אדם = 'to any person') fits perfectly.
אדם (א-ד-מ): Candidates: H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H123 'Edom'. Chose H120 — 'any person'.
נזק (נ-ז-ק): Candidates: H5142 'to suffer/inflict loss', H5143 'loss/damage'. Chose H5143 as the noun 'harm/damage'.
textual_notes: וה]פרשים[ — The brackets in the source indicate editorial uncertainty. פרשים could be 'horsemen/cavalry' (from פרש H6571) or possibly a corruption of פרושים 'Pharisees'. Given that the context parallels a scene where soldiers ask what to do, 'horsemen/soldiers' is more fitting.

משכיר0 יותיהם — This phrase is difficult. משכיר appears related to שכר (wages), and the 0 may indicate a scribal mark or corruption. יותיהם is unclear — possibly a possessive suffix construction. The overall sense appears to be 'from their wages' but the exact morphology is uncertain.
תחפצו — from חפץ 'to delight in, desire'. Not listed in candidates but clearly the verb root from context.

verses.literal: And the horsemen asked him saying what shall we do and Yochanan said do not desire evil to any man and do not do to him harm and be generous from your wages

verses.translation: All the people were thinking [or: supposing] that Yochanan might be Yeshua [the] Messiah [the anointed one].

translation_notes: העם (ע-מ): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. With the definite article ה, this is clearly 'the people' — H5971.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 (same). This is the proper name Yeshua/Jeshua.

משיח (מ-ש-י-ח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah', or root שיח H7878 'to ponder/converse'. Chose H4899 — 'anointed one/Messiah' fits the context of people wondering if Yochanan is the expected anointed figure.
textual_notes: סבורים is a post-biblical Hebrew term (from Aramaic סבר) meaning 'thinking/supposing'. It is not in the biblical Strong's lexicon, confirming later Hebrew composition.

The syntax ישוע משיח could be read as a title 'Yeshua the Messiah' or as two separate concepts 'the salvation [that is] the anointed one'. Given the narrative context — people wondering about identity — 'Yeshua the Messiah' as a title/name is most natural.

verses.literal: Thinking all the people that Yochanan would be Yeshua [the] anointed one

verses.translation: Yochanan responded and said to all of them: I immerse [baptize] you in water, but [one who is] mightier than I will come — I am not worthy to loosen the strap of his sandal. He will immerse you in the Holy Spirit [the breath of holiness] and in fire.

translation_notes: ענה (ע-נ-ה): Chose H6030 'to respond' — Yochanan is answering the people's speculation.
ואמר: Chose H559 'to say' — standard speech introduction.

textual_notes: The second half of this section (from אנו onward) breaks from the established שם היה pattern and appears to be a list of names without the formulaic introduction. Several names (מתתא, אליא, אלייה, אליי׳, אלים, מליא, מליאה, מנאנא, יודא, יודה) have no Strong's candidates provided, suggesting they may be variant spellings, Aramaic forms, or names not in the standard Hebrew lexicon.
אנו could be the pronoun 'we' (H580) or a proper name (possibly Enosh in a variant form). The genealogical context strongly favors a proper name.

The repetition of יודא/יהודה and יודה/יהודה may represent variant spellings of Judah being catalogued, or different individuals named Judah in the genealogy, or scribal annotations showing alternate forms.

This section appears to be a transition zone in the manuscript where the structured genealogical formula gives way to a less structured name list, possibly indicating a different source or scribal hand.

verses.translation: [His] name was Methuselah; [his] name was Enoch; [his] name was Jared; [his] name was Mahalalel; [[his] name was Kenan]

translation_notes: ירד (consonants ירד): Candidates: H3381 'to descend (verb)', H3382 'Jared (proper noun)'. In the genealogical pattern 'name was X,' only the proper noun Jared (H3382) is coherent. The genealogical sequence Mahalalel > Jared > Enoch > Methuselah matches known antediluvian lineage.
textual_notes: The final entry ]שם היה קינן[ is marked with brackets in the source text, indicating the scribe or a later editor considered this a restoration or uncertain reading. Kenan (H7018) also appeared in section 5, which may indicate overlapping genealogical segments or a textual join.

verses.literal: [The] name was Methuselah [the] name was Enoch [the] name was Jared [the] name was Mahalalel [the name was Kenan]

verses.translation: [His] name [or: identity] was Enosh; [his] name was Seth; [his] name was Adam; [the] name [or: identity, character] [of] the Mighty One [or: God, the Almighty]

translation_notes: אנוש (consonants אנוש): Candidates: H582 'a man/mankind', H583 'Enosh (son of Seth)'. In the genealogical sequence Adam > Seth > Enosh, the proper noun H583 is clearly indicated. Reading H582 'mankind' would break the genealogical pattern.
שת (consonants שת): Candidates: H8351 'tumult', H8352 'Seth (third son of Adam)', H8353 'six'. In the genealogical list between Adam and Enosh, only Seth (H8352) fits.

אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam (first man)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. In the genealogical line tracing back from Seth to the origin, Adam (H121) the first man is the clear reading. The sequence then moves to 'the name of God,' indicating Adam's origin from God.

האל (ה + אל): The ה is the definite article 'the.' Candidates for אל: H408 'not', H409 'not', H410 'strength/mighty/the Almighty/deity', H411 'these/those', H412 'these/those', H413 'near/to/among'. The genealogy has traced from Jesse back through the patriarchs to Adam; the final entry 'the name of the Mighty One' (H410 with the article) indicates Adam bore the name/identity of God — i.e., Adam [was of] God. H410 'the Almighty' produces the coherent climactic conclusion to the genealogy: humanity's origin in God.
textual_notes: The final phrase שם האל breaks from the pattern שם היה [name] by dropping the verb היה. This could mean: (1) '[the] name [of] the Mighty One' — indicating Adam was [of] God, a possessive construction; (2) '[the] name [was] the Mighty One' — with the verb implied; (3) a title: 'the Name of God' as a theological capstone to the genealogy. The absence of the verb היה distinguishes this final entry from all others, suggesting intentional structural emphasis marking the terminus of the lineage at God himself.

verses.literal: [The] name was Enosh [the] name was Seth [the] name was Adam [the] name [of] the Mighty One
